rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline built from the contract's physics and sensing rules. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the width at y = 0.03 m (ahead of the axle), at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 m. Spacing of 0.02 m is finer than the 25 mm tape width, so at least one or two sensors always see the line, and the signal varies smoothly as the line moves. Sensor size 0.012 m is a compromise between resolution and a wide footprint. Wheel track 0.12 m, wheel radius 0.03 m, mass 0.8 kg and body 0.12 x 0.18 m are mid-range, balancing turning authority, speed and stability. Wider body (0.12 m) gives a larger off-track allowance, which is a safety margin. Controller: sensor_weights are antisymmetric (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) so a positive signal (tape on the left) steers left, matching the contract. base_speed 1.6 targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish in under 3 s while keeping some margin for turns. kp 3.0 gives moderate steering (about 1050 PWM of wheel differential at full signal). ki 0.05 is small to avoid integral windup on long bends. kd 0.3 damps oscillation from the proportional term. line_loss is last_direction, so the robot keeps turning toward the side where it last saw the tape. Expected result: completion on the development tracks with modest oscillation. If the robot understeers on the slalom or oversteers with jitter, the next revision should adjust kp and kd. Hypotheses to check: (1) speed is not limited by the motor voltage drop at 1.6; (2) kd 0.3 is enough to damp the oscillation; (3) no line-loss events on the gentle oval. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion time, rms and max error, line-loss events and steering oscillation, so the next revision can separate tracking error from speed limits.
